question.problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(0,{\sigma }^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(|X|<7)=0.4648,$ find $\sigma ,$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

| $z$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.5\,$ | $\,0.6950\,$ | $\,0.6985\,$ | $\,0.7019\,$ |
| $\,0.6\,$ | $\,0.7291\,$ | $\,0.7324\,$ | $\,0.7357\,$ |
| $\,0.7\,$ | $\,0.7611\,$ | $\,0.7642\,$ | $\,0.7673\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
First, we express the given probability as

$$
P(|X|<7)=P(-7<X<7).
$$

Then, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-7<X<7) & =0.4648 \\ 2P(0<X<7) & =0.4648 \\ P(0<X<7) & =0.2324 \\ P(X<7)-P(X<0) & =0.2324 \\ P(X<7)-0.5 & =0.2324 \\ P(X<7) & =0.7324 \\ P(X\le 7) & =0.7324\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 7) & =0.7324 \\ P(Z\le \frac{7-0}{\sigma }) & =0.7324 \\ Φ(\frac{7}{\sigma }) & =0.7324 \\ \frac{7}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.7324)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.62)=0.7324\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.7324)=0.62.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{\sigma } & =0.62 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{7}{0.62} \\ \sigma  & ≈11.29.\end{aligned}
$$
